title: Add CPU thread for each device for parallel execution
body:
Github Issue: #5 

The main feature is parallel execution with CPU thread for each device.
* `Worker` class represents a CPU thread for model executions.
* `Work()` method in the `Worker` class is what each CPU thread runs.

### Workflow
* **Interpreter**: 
  * When `InvokeAll()` is called, 
    1. `Plan()` creates delegate ops.
    2. Each `Subgraph` in the `interpreter` is enqueued to the device queue.
    3. The interpreter waits until enqueued jobs to be done.

* **Planner**:
  * Current planner just provides methods and members to the interpreter and the workers.

* **Worker**:
  * When a `Worker` instance is created, a CPU thread running the `Work()` function is created.
  * Each worker waits until any request presents. When a job presents, `subgraph->invoke()` is called.
  * When the computation is done, the job is enqueued to an output queue in the planner. All the workers share the same output queue.

### Assumptions
* Model plan is still fixed.
  * So, when a model without DSP support is set to run on DSP, the job is sent to DSP's thread while the physical execution is held on CPU.
  * In this case, the execution may not be done properly.
* Planner is not a runtime component yet.
  * How a request is enqueued with central request queue, and how the planner recognizes when an invoke ends will be handled with the issue #18.

### Current Behavior
1. the planner creates delegate ops at the initial run. The plan is fixed.
2. Plan() is called by the main thread.

### Problem
* The planner is not a runtime component.
* Only the interpreter is able to call Plan(). The planner needs to know when a model inference ends for better planning logic.

### Expected Behavior
* Each model has subgraphs per device when the model is added.
* The planner runs in a different thread. The workers let the planner know when an inference ends.
* The planner has a central request queue and finished job queues.

title: Change how interpreter / subgraph handle delegates
body:
**Vanilla TFLite behavior**
`Interpreter` can have 1 graph/delegate.
Delegate initialization (`ModifyGraphWithDelegate()`) happens in
1. When the API user wants (Usually in an initialization phase)
2. At the end of the `Interpreter` construction in `InterpreterBuilder` (XNN, Flex delegate)

**Current behavior**
`Interpreter` have multiple delegates. (Initialized in a ctor)
`Subgraph` has 1 delegate.
Delegate initialization (`ModifyGraphWithDelegate()`) happens in `Planner->Plan()`.

**Expected behavior**
`Subgraph` should have all eligible delegates.
Delegate should be initialized when it's added to the subgraph.
`Planner->Plan()` should switch `current` delegate of the `Subgraph`.

**Note**
Some delegate eligibilities are available in `ModelPlan` (#14)

title: Prepare quantized tflite models available on GPU/DSP/TPU

milestone.title: Experiment Setup
milestone.description: Prepare for the multi-DNN experiments, such as TF Lite models and request generator.

body:
For more interesting experiments, models available on DSP, GPU are required.

As DSP needs INT8 quantized models (in case of GPU, INT8/FLOAT16), we need quantized `tflite` models:
* Current available
  * MobileNet V2
  * Inception V2/V3
  * YOLO, YOLO-tiny V3/V4
* Need quantization
  * Models in `mediapipe` repo
  * Object Detection (SSD)

### Note
~Succeeded in making INT8 quantized [YOLOv4-tiny.tflite](https://github.com/hunglc007/tensorflow-yolov4-tflite) model.~
Quantization fails due to the minimum filter size in a conv. layer. 

But,
* 3 `SPLIT` ops fall back to CPU, creating 4 GPU delegate ops.
* DSP Delegate op is not generated. (needs more investigation.)

Even though quantization is done, the lack of op coverage can be a big obstacle.

title: Simple execution planner
body:
Github issue: #4 

Add a simple planner component.

### Workflow
* When an `interpreter` is created, the interpreter creates GPU/DSP Delegate instances in `device_delegates_`. (If all models share the same delegate options, we do not have to create delegate ops for each `Subgraph`.)
* When `interpreter->InvokeAll()` is called, `Plan()` function is called. (Planning process is done for the first invocation in this implementation.)
* `Plan()` assigns a model to a device in a round-robin manner and creates a delegate op for each model.
* Models are still sequentially executed.

### Future Work
Issues #9, #10

body:
Currently, `interpreter->context_` refers to the context of `primary_subgraph`, as there is only one `Subgraph` in the original code.

As we have to manage more than one TF Lite model, we have to modify what the `context_` indicates.
1. Make a vector of contexts. (`i`th context is `i`th model's context.)
2. Let `Subgraph`s share only one context. Then, we may not have to change how `interpreter` is using `context_`.

Methods using `context_` in the interpreter are not used in the benchmark tool, so currently there is no problem running the benchmark tool.

title: Sequential multi-model run in TF Lite Interpreter
body:
Issue #1

This PR adds a sequential multi-model run feature in the TF Lite interpreter. 
* Models are added as elements of `interpreter->subgraphs_`.
* Modified codes in `tools/benchmark` directory enable sequential multi-model run in the `benchmark tool`. 

### Workflow
1. Add models to the interpreter through `interpreter_builder`. ([code](https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/compare/multi-model?expand=1#diff-5e52c34dca4078ca18facf285e6ade5eR605))
    * `interpreter->AddSubgraphs(1)` creates space for a new model.
    * `AddSubgraphs` is called when `AddSubgraph` is called. (Not in the constructor of an interpreter.)
2. Emplace back each model as the last element of `subgraphs_`.  ([code](https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/compare/multi-model?expand=1#diff-a1383c0e54f638b4fc6f14344497b842R632))
3. Allocate memory for each model in `interpreter->AllocateTensor()`. ([code](https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/compare/multi-model?expand=1#diff-a5cdd9573a0b4fba01ee0b15fe1769e9R183))
4. Invoke models in the interpreter. ([code](https://github.com/mrsnu/tflite/compare/multi-model?expand=1#diff-a5cdd9573a0b4fba01ee0b15fe1769e9R277))
